articles.title_zh: Gasgoo Daily: Zhou Xiaoying: China’s Auto Industry Enters a Critical Restructuring Phase; Fu Yuwu: Build China’s Auto Industry Soft Power, Foster New Ecosystem & Value; Jetta M6 Hits the Market
articles.content_orig:
Gasgoo Daily presents a selection of the latest developments from China's automotive industry. Here are the key stories in this edition.
Zhou Xiaoying: China's Auto Industry Enters a Critical Restructuring Phase At the 14th Automobile & Environment Innovation Forum and the 8th Gasgoo Awards ceremony "China Solutions, Global Value", Gasgoo CEO and editor-in-chief Zhou Xiaoying shared her take on the industry's shift from scale to value. She said growth in sales volume is no longer translating into value creation, as the industry enters a period of structural change. The gap between a cooling domestic market and strong overseas demand is widening. Across the industry, higher volumes aren't bringing in more revenue, and higher revenue isn't bringing in more profit. Export growth has helped, but it can't make up for weak profits at home. Zhou added that the four-year price war is still going. It has reshuffled market share, but it hasn't created lasting value—and it can't go on forever.
Fu Yuwu: Build China's Auto Industry Soft Power, Foster New Ecosystem & Value Speaking on Oct. 23 at the 14th Automobile & Environment Innovation Forum and the 8th Gasgoo Awards ceremony "China Solutions, Global Value", Fu Yuwu, honorary chairman of both the Society of Automotive Engineers of China and the China Automotive Talent Research Association, said the industry must tackle critical technologies while also building its soft power. That will take closer collaboration between academia, research and industry to create a new ecosystem and new value.
Jetta M6 Hits the Market: A 35-Year-Old People's Car Brand Goes Electric The Jetta M6 hit the market in Chengdu on Oct. 22. The 465 Pro, 555 Max and 555 Ultra are priced at ¥79,800, ¥89,800 and ¥99,800, respectively—all under ¥100,000. Jetta sums up its positioning in eight Chinese characters: "Under ¥100,000, fully equipped from the get-go." The launch carries two big implications for Jetta. The M6 is the brand's first locally developed all-electric model and the first product from FAW-Volkswagen Jetta Technology Co. For a 35-year-old household name with 5.3 million customers, it marks the start of a new electric and smart-vehicle era, alongside its continued development of gas-powered cars. For joint-venture brands as a whole, the M6 offers a way to fight back in the ¥100,000-and-under EV market, where Chinese brands have taken the lead: pair German quality with Chinese tech.

articles.title_orig: North Korea has opened up bridges to Russia and China – in which direction will it go?
articles.title_zh: North Korea has opened up bridges to Russia and China – in which direction will it go?
articles.content_orig:
Kim Yo-jong, sister of Kim Jong-un, issues warning after inspecting border fortifications against backdrop of rising tensions
Propaganda loudspeakers aimed at South Korea will be ready to restart within days along the entire border, Kim Yo-jong, the powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, has said amid a worsening of ties between the two countries.
The statement, carried by the state news agency KCNA on Thursday, came a day after she said the loudspeakers would be in operation along the whole border from some time in October.
Both North and South Korea have historically used giant loudspeakers to broadcast propaganda across the border, with the North in recent years playing haunting bestial howls, and the South opting for K-pop music ​and news criticising Pyongyang.
If the broadcasts resume, they would be the first loudspeaker exchange across the border in 16 months. South Korean president Lee Jae Myung suspended broadcasts from the southern side just days into his presidency in June 2025 to ease tensions with Pyongyang, and the military dismantled the speakers that August.
At a briefing on Thursday, a defence ministry spokesperson in Seoul said that if North Korea went ahead, “naturally there would have to be a proportional measure”, but made clear no decision had been made.
The joint chiefs of staff said routine maintenance of the North’s loudspeakers had been observed before Kim Yo-jong’s statements.
Tensions between the two Koreas have risen since September, when a landmine blast south of the military demarcation line injured three South Korean soldiers, two of them seriously.
Seoul and the UN command – which oversees the 1953 armistice that halted but did not end the Korean war – concluded it was a North Korean anti-personnel mine and an armistice violation. Pyongyang denied responsibility and called the incident a “self-staged farce”.
The loudspeaker threat comes as North Korea continues to fortify its side of the border. Since Kim Jong-un declared that the two Koreas were “two states hostile to each other” in December 2023, North Korea has laid mines, strung barbed wire and erected anti-tank barriers along the border.
On Wednesday, Kim Yo-jong inspected several fortification points along the border with Pak Jong-chon, a marshal and adviser to Pyongyang’s defence ministry.
The border had been “clearly blocked and turned into a fortress more thoroughly”, she said, adding that Kim Jong-un had told her it “should be a permanent line never to be crossed”.
Seoul says North Korean troops have repeatedly crossed the military demarcation line, the 250km line dividing the two Koreas, during the construction work, prompting South Korean soldiers to issue warnings over loudspeakers and fire warning shots.
North Korea has called the warning shots and broadcasts provocations by “armed rogues”.

articles.title_orig: I Drove The Electric BMW X5. It Makes The Gas Version A Tough Sell.
articles.title_zh: I Drove The Electric BMW X5. It Makes The Gas Version A Tough Sell.
articles.content_orig:
The fifth-generation BMW X5 is here, and for the first time ever it comes in a dizzying array of powertrain options: gas, diesel, plug-in hybrid, hydrogen (yes, seriously), and, the subject of today’s review: electric.
All the X5s are identical inside and out: same clean look, same distinctive X-shaped headlights, same screens, same high-class cabin. So why pick one over the other? After driving both the combustion X5 and the electric iX5 for a day in Southern California, I think BMW has made an exceptional case for its buyers to go electric. The iX5 provides gobs of range, super-fast charging, dazzling tech, and a more pleasant driving experience than the gas version.

*Lemonade and the FSD discount are available in select states, learn more at the link above.
Perhaps more than ever, the decision comes down to one simple question: Can you live without the theater of a combustion engine? If so, the iX5 deserves your attention.
[Full disclosure: BMW covered my travel and lodging in Newport Beach, California, so I could drive the new iX5.]
The iX5 is the latest of BMW’s Neue Klasse vehicles, joining the new iX3 crossover and i3 sedan. It’s one of the most important too; while BMW made its name as a sports-sedan company, the X5 and X3 are its bread and butter in the U.S. So the X5 going all-electric (at least as an option) is a big deal both for BMW and for America’s EV options.
The iX5 uses BMW’s sixth-generation EV motors and batteries , and has the biggest battery pack ever fitted to a BMW production car, at 144 kWh. While the iX3 and i3 use 4695 cells—that is, ones that are 46 millimeters wide and 95 mm tall—the iX5 uses 46120s, giving it extra energy capacity and a huge amount of range. The battery uses a cell-to-pack format without bulky modules. (It’s not a cell-to-body design like the other Neue Klasse cars, BMW told me, since the X5’s chassis also has to accommodate other powertrains.)
When BMW first announced the iX5’s specs earlier this year, it targeted an EPA range of 435 miles, but that figure has since grown. At last week’s drive event, BMW reps said they’re now estimating an EPA range of 450 miles , which would put the iX5 in a very small club . Michael Ahlers, the head of the X5 project, told me BMW realized that 400 miles of range was the sweet spot where potential buyers stop complaining about not having enough.
Pair with that an 800-volt architecture and some of the highest-powered charging in a U.S. production car, and you get—on paper, at least—an EV with far fewer compromises than those that came before it. BMW says the iX5 can charge at up to 460 kilowatts (you’d be hard-pressed to even find a station that can dispense that) and recharge from 10%-80% in 22 minutes. That equates to over 300 miles of estimated EPA range added in not very much time.
Rounding out the EV specs, every iX5 will come with bidirectional charging capability that can be routed through various attachments: a vehicle-to-load adapter with three 110-volt outlets and a vehicle-to-home adapter that turns the SUV into a home-backup battery.
The iX5 60 xDrive will start at $79,800, plus a $1,450 destination charge. That’s $7,700 more than the gas-powered X5 40 xDrive. But for the added outlay you get a more powerful, quicker car with home-backup capability and, I’d argue, a more enjoyable driving experience. The X5 rolls out starting this month, while the iX5 hits U.S. dealerships in early 2027.
When I drove the iX3 last year , I came impressed with how agile, smooth, and quiet it was. With the iX5, it’s largely the same story, just in a noticeably bigger and heavier package. The SUV’s 570 horsepower and 593 pound-feet of torque give it more than enough zip, helping mask its weight.
Even at highway speeds, the iX5 feels like it has plenty more to give—and unlike in the combustion version, power comes on immediately. Driving the two powertrains back to back gave me that much more appreciation for the effortless, punchy performance you get in the EV at virtually any speed. (On paper, the iX5 is rated to hit 60 in 4.4 seconds, while the xDrive 40 is rated at 4.8 seconds.)
Sure, the X5 40 xDrive brings the drama and raucous experience of a gas engine, but you also have to deal with gear changes and turbo lag. Clearly, I’m no gas-car enthusiast and I’m preaching to the choir here, but I’ve come to prefer the electric way—just put your foot down, and you’re off at full beans.
Put someone else who’s EV-curious in the driver’s seat of both options, and I think many would come to the same conclusion. It’s why survey after survey show that once someone buys an EV, they’re pretty much hooked.
On twisty mountain roads, I found the iX5 settled around corners and decently engaging to drive. The giant battery in the floor, while making the SUV feel heavier than the gas one, also provides a lower center of gravity. An X5’s real daily duty, though, is puttering around town or cruising casually on the highway, and the iX5 gets high marks for its performance in either environment. On long stints, it was quiet, comfortable, and overall a pleasant place to pass the time.
I also got to try out BMW’s latest hands-free driver-assistance tech on this trip, both in the X5 and the new 7 Series. It works great. The system holds a lane confidently, doesn’t nag you unnecessarily, and asks you to confirm automatic lane changes by glancing at the driver-side mirror to double check for traffic. It also features collaborative steering, so you can reposition the car within its lane quite freely without fully taking over.
I’ll start with the good. BMW’s Panoramic Vision display, that slim bit of screen running across the entire car just below the windshield, is one of the best new car features I’ve seen lately in an auto industry whose mantra has become “more screen.” We should all be glad it’s not limited to EVs, but rather will land in gas BMWs as well. (And a hydrogen one, if that floats your boat.)
The display is remarkably high-contrast, making it legible even when the sun is streaming into the cabin or when viewed through sunglasses. It puts basic driving info like your gear, drive mode, range, and speed above the steering wheel and right in your line of sight to the road. The iX5 offers a crisp head-up display too, but I’d argue you really don’t need it. The leftmost gauge-cluster bit of the Panoramic Vision display includes turn-by-turn directions, making the most useful part of a HUD redundant.
The rest of the screen can be configured to include just about anything else you might want to check at a glance. Those include the date and time, current weather conditions, and power output. Plus, BMW threw in some stuff that’s just for fun. The screen now includes the option of several “art cars,” BMWs from years past with funky designs. So you can have an E30 M3 or a Z1 keep you company from the dash.
The main display is nice enough to use, too, and its off-kilter look lends the cabin a fresher feel than pure rectangular designs do. It’s quick to respond to taps and swipes, and the design is crisp and easy to read. There’s a quick-access menu accessible from the portion closest to your right hand for things like door locks and opening the trunk. The home screen features the map, plus a vertical carousel of key functions lining the left-hand side of the screen. In all, it has a far more modern and Silicon-Valley feel than BMW’s previous iDrive system.
But the UI could use some fine-tuning. For example, the home button at the bottom of the display only appears when you’re not on the home screen. Othe

articles.title_orig: Xbox’s first chief operating officer is out after just a few months
articles.title_zh: Xbox’s first chief operating officer is out after just a few months
articles.content_orig:
Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft after 21 years.
Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft after 21 years.
Xbox’s first chief operating officer (COO) is leaving after the new role was created just a few months ago. Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft today, according to an internal Xbox memo seen by The Verge . Chiang has been at Microsoft for 21 years, serving as the head of Minecraft before being promoted to Xbox chief operating officer in July.
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced Chiang’s departure in a surprisingly short memo today. “Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft today. I’m grateful for her years of service and wish her well,” said Sharma. As Chiang is departing today, her immediate responsibilities are being split up between other Xbox leaders for now, and Sharma notes that “We’ll share more on COO leadership as plans are finalized.”
That sounds like the COO position isn’t going away after just a few months, but it’s not clear why Chiang is departing after such a short stint in the role. At the time of Chiang’s promotion, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma described the new chief operating officer role as a first for Xbox, “with end-to-end P&L responsibility across content, hardware, platform, and services.” The role was created as part of Xbox’s big “reset.”
Chiang reported directly to Sharma, and was promoted to “bring our businesses together under one operating model, making sure we make clear investment decisions, learn from our successes and failures, and hold ourselves accountable for results.”
Chiang departs amid rumors that Xbox is preparing more layoffs this month, in November, and January. The sudden and short memo from Sharma, coupled with Chiang’s responsibilities being assigned to other Xbox leaders, makes it seem like this wasn’t a resignation.
I asked Microsoft to comment on Chiang’s departure, and the company refused to discuss the circumstances of her exit. “We don’t discuss individual personnel matters,” says Kari Perez, Xbox vice president of communications. “We’re grateful for Helen’s years of service and wish her well.”

articles.title_orig: Alleged Chinese agent Wanying Zhang pleads not guilty in Los Angeles courtroom
articles.title_zh: Alleged Chinese agent Wanying Zhang pleads not guilty in Los Angeles courtroom
articles.content_orig:
A Southern California realtor accused of being a Chinese foreign agent pleaded not guilty to the allegations in a Los Angeles federal courtroom Friday.
Wanying Zhang, 34, appeared in a white jumpsuit and shackles, speaking only to deny charges that she surveilled the Taiwanese president's son in a Seattle suburb in September 2025.
The plea puts the case on track for a trial that will require the Justice Department to lay out its evidence of the allegations she conspired with Chinese intelligence officials for what prosecutors called a spy mission.
She was arrested earlier this month at L.A. International Airport while attempting to board a flight to China. She has been charged with one count of acting in the U.S. as an unregistered agent of the Chinese government.
Zhang's husband, Edric Ding, had appeared in earlier court hearings. The couple have been realtors together at the same firm in Irvine, California.
But Ding did not appear at the short hearing on Friday. This is after prosecutors claimed in a recent court filing that Zhang was having an affair with a man who accompanied her on the alleged surveillance mission to Washington state last year. CBS has identified him as Fatai Miao, a construction entrepreneur who recently left Southern California on a one-way ticket to China.
Miao's son told CBS News he does not believe his father was working for the Chinese government, and Miao has not been charged with any crime.
The judge set a pretrial hearing for Nov. 12. The trial is scheduled to begin Nov. 30 at a federal courthouse in Santa Ana, California, and will last an estimated four days.
Both prosecutors and Zhang's attorney, Craig Harbaugh, declined to comment on Friday.

articles.title_orig: Argentina drops investigation into President Milei over crypto fraud
articles.title_zh: Argentina drops investigation into President Milei over crypto fraud
articles.content_orig:
A criminal investigation into Argentine President Javier Milei and his sister's links to a cryptocurrency scandal has been dropped.
The case against Milei and his sister Karina Milei was dismissed by federal judge Marcelo Martinez de Giorgi at the request of prosecutors, court records show.
The Argentinian president had denied promoting the newly launched cryptocoin $Libra , which collapsed shortly after he mentioned it in a social media post in February 2025.
He said he had acted "in good faith" when the cryptocurrency rose in value before crashing and causing huge losses for the majority of its investors. Milei is yet to respond to news of the case being dropped.
Dismissing the case, the judge said "the reported events do not fall under a legal category", and concluded that no "criminally relevant deception" had been proven.
Accusations of fraud arose when Milei posted on X, formerly Twitter, about the $Libra coin, which he said at the time would help fund small businesses and start-ups.
The cryptocurrency's price subsequently shot up when the Argentine president shared a link to buy it.
But, within a few hours, he deleted his post and the crypto nosedived in value, losing investors most of their money.
It led opposition members of Congress to plan impeachment proceedings, while some online accused Milei of a "rug pull" - where promoters of a cryptocurrency draw in buyers, only to stop trading activity and make off with the money raised from sales.
The Argentinian president, though, insisted: "I didn't promote it, I merely shared it" in an interview with local media Todo Noticias'.
The presidential office insisted that Milei was in no way involved in the development of $Libra and announced that the Anti-Corruption Office would determine if the president had acted improperly.
Milei himself defended deleting his post, saying that at the time he did not know "the details of the project and after learning about it, I decided not to continue promoting it".
And, in a TV interview, he insisted that those who invested in $Libra had done so "voluntarily" and knew of the risks.

articles.title_orig: US discreetly moves diplomats and families from multiple Middle Eastern countries as escalation fears grow
articles.title_zh: US discreetly moves diplomats and families from multiple Middle Eastern countries as escalation fears grow
articles.content_orig:
The United States is rushing to move some diplomats and their family members from posts in the Middle East as the threat of regional escalation looms, according to multiple sources familiar with the matter.
The departures have been described as a frustrating and chaotic déjà vu, as many of those leaving had only recently returned to their posts after being ordered out during the height of the Iran war.
“To say it has been chaotic is an understatement,” said one US diplomat, explaining that the financial support they have been offered to date does not cover the costs for moving their entire family from the region. Many of those families had scrambled then to leave their homes in the Middle East in the early weeks of the war and find new housing and schools for their kids. Now, many are having to do the same again, with what they say is potentially less financial support from the State Department.
“This echoes the chaos families experienced earlier this year. Some had barely settled back in before being told to leave again,” Nikki Gamer, the spokesperson for the American Foreign Service Association, told CNN. “They are understandably upset, confused, and angry.”
Later Friday, a State Department official confirmed that all US direct hire personnel and their families “are getting per diem allowances and support for lodging and schools, with per diem allowances consistent with government rates of where they are geographically in the country.”
The adjustments come as the Iranian-backed Houthis have increased their attacks on Saudi Arabia – hostilities which the State Department has repeatedly warned “have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area.”
They also come as US President Donald Trump has suggested he could relaunch strikes against Iran after the midterms, and as sources said Israel has lobbied – unsuccessfully for now – for more immediate action.
The State Department this week ordered the departure of non-emergency personnel and all family members from Saudi Arabia. Officials said the ordered departure was done in response to the Houthi escalations.
At the same time, it has been quietly adjusting its staffing caps at multiple other embassies in the Middle East, including Jordan, Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, and Lebanon, sources told CNN.
A State Department official confirmed to CNN that Lebanon, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, and Jordan “will see temporary changes to staffing levels under restricted operations.” They said there are no changes to personnel in Kuwait or Bahrain, which suggest they are not over their staffing caps.
“Under Restricted Operations Status, staffing levels are constantly evaluated and adjusted,” the official said.
Unlike the Saudi Arabia ordered departure, the movements from these embassies have not been publicly announced. The State Department has stressed that those embassies, unlike Saudi Arabia, have not changed status and remain on “restricted operations” status. Even when there is no formal change in status, there can still be a change in staffing within the “restricted operations” status.
“There’s a very Groundhog Day vibe,” a source in Amman said of some embassy staff being asked to leave the Jordanian capital again.
Not all of the embassies allowed children to return to the posts, but most allowed spouses to come back. Now, the family members are leaving those embassies to which they have only recently been allowed to return – but unlike earlier this year, sources say family members are not being given the same financial support.
Communication and coordination around the departures from the department’s headquarters in Foggy Bottom to foreign service officers in the field is “just as much of a shit show” as early on in the Iran war, said one source familiar with the departures.
In the days around the adjustments, there were concerns among foreign service officers about whether the State Department will give their families “per diem” allowances for relocating to the US, the source said, noting that some embassies haven’t had the planning meetings or town halls with staff that are typical before departures.
“A lot of people are hearing about it through the news instead of their leadership at post,” the source added.
The American Foreign Service Association, the union representing foreign service officers, said it is hearing accounts “of bureaucratic ping-pong.”
“Families that had barely returned to their posts and re-enrolled their children in school are being told to prepare to evacuate again without being advised as to what level of financial support they can count on,” it said in a statement Thursday.
Gamer, the spokesperson for AFSA, told CNN that “families outside Saudi Arabia have told AFSA they are being directed to leave without confirmed housing assistance or per diem.” They have been told this is because their embassies are not changing status from “restricted operations.”
Families often rely on those allowances to help them find housing and cover the unexpected costs associated with being uprooted from their homes abroad, especially if their diplomatic family member is remaining at the embassy as an essential worker.
“Families deserve to know how they will pay for a place to live before they board a plane,” Gamer said.
The State Department official said, “We understand how hard being on Restricted Operations Status, Authorized Departure, or Ordered Departure is for our diplomatic staff and their families.”
“We are committed to using every tool available to help families navigate this difficult time, including the added expenses and school enrollment,” they said. “We are communicating directly with staff affected by these latest changes and will have more to say in the days ahead.”
This story has been updated with additional details.

articles.title_orig: Duchess of Sussex was told of ‘disturbing allegations’ against her father in 2018
articles.title_zh: Duchess of Sussex was told of ‘disturbing allegations’ against her father in 2018
articles.content_orig:
Meghan reveals she was made aware of ‘disturbing allegations’ against him in 2018 by Met police
The Duchess of Sussex has said she is “deeply distressed” over accusations involving child sexual abuse images against her estranged father, Thomas Markle Sr, and revealed she was made aware of “disturbing allegations” against him in 2018 by the Metropolitan police.
Meghan issued a statement after the Sun newspaper published claims that her half-brother Thomas Markle Jr alleged he had found a stash of images belonging to their father at his former home in the Philippines.
In an interview with the Daily Mail, Markle Sr denied possessing child sexual abuse images, calling the accusations “sick lies”.
It is understood that authorities in the UK previously told Meghan that allegations made about her father in a 2018 letter sent to Scotland Yard, and subsequently shared with her by the police, were being investigated.
Meghan was informed by the Met of the allegations in the summer shortly after her wedding, it is believed.
In a statement through her spokesperson, Meghan said: “I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed.
“In 2018, a letter was sent to the Metropolitan police and Royalty and Specialist Protection [Rasp]. That letter was subsequently shared with me. It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated.
“I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications’ distortion over the years, any distance from my father, and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them. I trusted that the authorities were doing the same for other families.
“Although the breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine, my sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children.”
Sources said although Meghan was made aware of the allegations in 2018, she had been unable to speak publicly to avoid jeopardising any future investigation and because speaking out could have resulted in legal action against her.
The 2018 letter was understood to have been shared with Meghan by the Rasp unit within the Met police.
It is understood the Met has not previously investigated Markle Sr, nor is it currently doing so. The force said it was making internal inquiries regarding officers from Rasp being involved in the passing on of a letter.
A Met spokesperson said: “We are aware of media reports that officers from the Met’s royalty and specialist protection command were involved in the passing on of a letter in 2018. We are undertaking inquiries internally in an effort to confirm this.”
Markle Sr has been estranged from the duchess since he failed to attend her wedding to Prince Harry on health grounds, and he has never met his grandchildren Prince Archie, seven, and Princess Lilibet, five.
The Sun reported that Markle Jr told detectives in the Philippines he had discovered “hundreds, if not thousands” of child sexual abuse images on computers and mobile phones stored in four large boxes at the home in Cebu where Markle Sr was living until he returned to the US in May after having a stroke.
Markle Jr, 60, said he had also contacted the FBI in the US, the Sun reported.
The FBI said in a statement: “The FBI is aware of the allegations and will provide support, as appropriate, to the Philippine authorities. We will also investigate any related allegations of federal violations of US law.”
The undersecretary for the Philippines’ justice department, Nicholas Ty, told the BBC the matter was being investigated by a human trafficking and child sexual exploitation taskforce in Cebu.
The interior secretary, Jonvic Remulla, separately told the BBC that national police had secured Markle Sr’s computer to conduct a comprehensive digital forensic examination. Remulla said it would take “one week to get the forensic [results]”.
Meghan’s father has denied possessing child sexual abuse images, telling the Daily Mail that the accusations were “sick lies”.
He told the newspaper that the computers had not been in his possession since he left Rosarito, Mexico, with his son in January 2025 and moved to the Philippines “for a fresh start”.
Speaking from a rehabilitation centre in Florida, where he is learning to walk with a prosthetic limb after his left leg was amputated because of a blood clot, he told the Mail: “I’m shocked, I’m hurt and I’m very upset that my son is making these accusations against me. I could never do what I’m being accused of. It’s the worst thing anyone could accuse me of.
“This is bullshit. It’s just a bunch of lies. It’s sick. I have no idea why Tom is trying to destroy me with these lies.”
Meghan’s half-sister Samantha Markle has defended their father, accusing her brother Markle Jr of “making up lies” to make money.
She told the Mail: “There is no merit in these disgusting allegations whatsoever and my brother is disgusting for making them up. He wants to destroy our dad. Shame on him.”
She alleged her brother made the allegations days after their father cut off his funds, “and once the money stopped he made up the most outrageous lies he could to make money from the media”.
She alleged the computers were not in her father’s possession for two years and he could have been set up. “That leaves a lot of room for tampering,” she said.

articles.title_orig: Ebola: Kenya records second death as 65-year-old woman succumbs
articles.title_zh: Ebola: Kenya records second death as 65-year-old woman succumbs
articles.content_orig:
Kenya has announced its second Ebola death, as the virus outbreak spreads from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) to several parts of Africa.
The Kenyan Ministry of Health said on Friday that the latest death was that of a 65-year-old woman who had developed symptoms during quarantine and was a close relative of a Kenyan man who died ⁠⁠of Ebola earlier this month.
The ministry added that Kenya currently has seven Ebola cases receiving treatment at two isolation facilities.
All the cases are within “one cluster, with no evidence of community spread”, it added.
Kenya’s first Ebola case was identified this month in a man who travelled from DRC to Kenya and died at ‌‌a Nairobi hospital on October 5.
Since then, Kenyan authorities have traced 135 contacts, all of whom were placed in quarantine, with nine cases confirmed, including the two patients who died.
The DRC declared its 17th Ebola outbreak in May and has since reported more than 9,000 cases and more than 4,600 deaths. The deadly disease has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the past 50 years.
The current outbreak has now been reported in four countries across eastern, central ⁠⁠and western Africa, giving it the widest geographic spread of any Ebola outbreak on the continent to date.
On Tuesday, Nigeria became the fourth ⁠⁠African country to report an Ebola case. Nigerian Health Minister Muhammad ⁠⁠Ali Pate said on Friday that an analysis showed the case was closely ‌‌related to the virus detected in the index case ⁠⁠in Kenya.
Uganda announced on Saturday that travellers ⁠⁠with a history of ⁠⁠travel to DRC would not be permitted to transit through the East African ⁠⁠nation.
Uganda had recorded 20 people infected, almost all of whom had travelled from DRC, and two deaths before being declared Ebola-free in August.

articles.title_orig: AI Trade Stumbles Again as Investors Rediscover Treasury Haven
articles.title_zh: AI Trade Stumbles Again as Investors Rediscover Treasury Haven
articles.content_orig:
The gap is closing, but the opportunity is in new leaders, not broken AI names.
You've reached your free article limit
You've read 0 of 1 free Pro articles.
I’ve been discussing the two-tiered nature of this market and the gap in performance between AI-related names and the rest of the market for months now. My thesis was that this gap would eventually start to close, but we couldn’t be sure how that would occur. Today we had a significant advance in the narrowing of this gap.
The easiest way to see it is in the indices. The Nasdaq 100 dropped about 2.9%, the Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF ( MAGS ) fell 3.5% and the VanEck Semiconductor ETF ( SMH ) fell 5.8%. At the same time, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was flat, and the iShares Russell 2000 ETF ( IWM ) had a small gain. Most notably, the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF ( RSP ) was up 0.7%. Despite the carnage in the AI group, breadth was 47% positive.
That is the most dramatic reversal we have seen between the two tiers of the market since this split began. The question now is whether it continues, and if it does, whether we will see continued severe pressure on the AI sector or whether it will chop around while the rest of the market gains momentum.
No one knows the answer to that. We need to stay focused on the charts and look for those that are building support and showing signs of relative strength. Lots of folks are going to try to bottom fish the broken AI names, but I believe you would be better off looking for new leaders rather than trying to catch a bottom in the old ones.
We had another rotation on Thursday as well, between equities and bonds. Bonds were a major problem for the market for a while as rates moved higher, but as the leading AI names struggled, bonds regained their status as a safe haven. Bonds were strong on Thursday as money that left the AI sector looked for a nice, safe yield.
Ironically, the trigger for this severe rotational action was seemingly good earnings reports from Meta Platforms ( META ) and Tesla ( TSLA ). Investors are fearful that the massive investment needed in computing power may not deliver the payoff that is being priced into these stocks. On Thursday, the whole sector was sold, but there will be opportunity as the market sorts out which companies can navigate the capital markets and protect profit margins most effectively.
My game plan has been to watch for this rotational action to gain traction and to focus on the best charts as it evolves. That isn’t as simple or as easy as it sounds, since there is elevated volatility and a lot of trading action that has no relationship to fundamentals. I do feel optimistic about the many opportunities that are developing, but it is going to take some hard work and patience to generate profits.
Have a good evening. I’ll see you tomorrow.
At the time of publication, DePorre had no positions in any securities mentioned.
By James "Rev Shark" DePorre

articles.title_zh: Over 4 million tubes of toothpaste have been recalled, including kids brands — here’s what you need to know
articles.content_orig:
NBC Selected independently determines what we cover and recommend. When you click on or buy through our links, we earn a commission. Learn more .
More than 4.3 million tubes of fluoride toothpaste — many of them kid-themed , in flavors like bubble gum, strawberry and watermelon — have been voluntarily recalled nationwide after the Food and Drug Administration flagged manufacturing problems at the facility that made them.
The recall covers several brands sold under licensed character names, along with a handful of lesser-known labels, and includes tubes with expiration dates stretching into mid-2028, meaning some of the affected toothpaste could be sitting in your medicine cabinet right now.
No illnesses or injuries have been reported. Still, the FDA says families should check lot numbers and expiration dates to see whether their toothpaste is part of the recall. Below, I break down exactly which products are affected, how to tell if you have one and what to do next.
The FDA announced the recall of more than 4.3 million tubes of fluoride toothpaste distributed nationwide because of current good manufacturing practice deviations. Those are federal standards meant to ensure products are made consistently and safely, so a deviation means the manufacturing process didn’t meet requirements, not necessarily that the toothpaste itself is harmful.
The voluntary recall was initiated on September 10 by Pritam International Private Limited, an India-based manufacturer, and the FDA classified it as Class II recall on October 19. A Class II recall is for products that could cause temporary or medically reversible health problems, where the chance of serious harm is considered unlikely. The FDA notice did not report any illnesses or injuries linked to the recalled toothpaste.
Many of the affected tubes were marketed to kids. The recalled products include toothpaste sold under the Brush Buddies, Crayola, Hot Wheels and My Little Pony brands, in flavors such as bubble gum, strawberry, watermelon, peppermint, sweet mint and cool mint. They were distributed by Ashtel Studios Inc. of Ontario, California, and come in 3.5-ounce and 4-ounce tubes, plus a two-pack of 3.5-ounce tubes.
Affected products carry expiration dates from November 2026 through June 2028, and consumers should check the lot numbers and expiration dates on the FDA’s recall notice to see whether theirs is included.
The FDA’s recall notice doesn’t include specific instructions for consumers, and neither the manufacturer nor the distributor has issued public guidance on returns or refunds. Until they do, the safest move is to stop using the toothpaste immediately and toss it out. Start by checking the brand, lot number and expiration date on your tube against the FDA’s recall notice; if it matches, discard it and switch to a different fluoride toothpaste so your family’s brushing routine isn’t interrupted.
Hang on to your receipt or take a photo of the packaging before tossing it, in case a refund process is announced later. No illnesses or injuries have been reported, but if you or your child used the product and have any concerns, you should contact your dentist or doctor immediately.
The below toothpastes were not recalled and have at least a four-star average rating from thousands of customers.
My kids absolutely love this toothpaste — in fact, it is the only one they will use. The fruity flavor makes brushing less of a chore, while fluoride fights cavities and calcium and silica gently clean teeth. It’s approved by the American Dental Association (ADA), free of artificial colors, flavors, and preservatives, and suitable for children ages 2 and up.
This toothpaste’s bright blue, sparkly color will delight kids. Plus, the fluoride formula fights cavities while staying gentle on enamel, and it carries the ADA Seal of Acceptance . It is suitable for children ages 2 and up, with adult supervision.
If you can’t decide on which hello kids’ flavor your little one will love, grab this variety pack that lets them sample all three and pick a favorite. Each toothpaste comes in a brightly colored tube with an easy flip cap that sits flat when closed, so it stands neatly on the bathroom counter.
If you had one of the adult toothpastes in the recall, Crest Pro-Health Advanced is a reliable replacement from a brand you already know. It’s an antibacterial fluoride toothpaste that fights plaque bacteria and supports healthy gums. It also helps whiten teeth and strengthen enamel.

articles.title_orig: Updated Google privacy policy says your Gmail might be used for advertising
articles.title_zh: Updated Google privacy policy says your Gmail might be used for advertising
articles.content_orig:
Using Google’s products and services has always been fundamentally precarious—doing so gives the world’s largest advertising company a lot of juicy personal data. Google has long said it won’t use the sensitive data from products like Gmail, Drive, and Photos for ad personalization, but a change to the company’s privacy policy appears to dismantle that firewall.
On October 16, Google issued an update to its privacy policy , spotted by Android Authority . The ad personalization section used to include a clear limit on data from certain apps. “We don’t show you personalized ads based on your content from Drive, Gmail, or Photos,” the document said. Now, Google has updated it with the following language.
This equivocation opens the door to using data from apps like Gmail and Photos in ads when it’s shared with other Google services, and it just so happens Google has a mechanism for doing that, with Personal Intelligence. The company released Personal Intelligence in early 2026 , allowing users to hand data from multiple apps to Google AI products. The idea is that the added context from your existing data will lead to better AI answers, but it’s also proving to be a privacy minefield.
Personal Intelligence connects your data to the Gemini app but also to features like AI Mode search. While the Gemini app does not currently have ads, you may see sponsored content in AI search tools. Google’s changes to the privacy policy appear to acknowledge that data shared with AI search via Personal Intelligence could, therefore, contribute to ad personalization.
According to Google, this clarification still doesn’t mean ads are “based directly” on your personal data. Here’s the company’s full statement:
“Connecting your apps is entirely opt-in. Ads will continue to be relevant to things like your query, the context of the response and your interests. Ads will not be based directly on your Gmail inbox or Photos library, and as always, sensitive information will not be used to tailor ads.”
Google’s statement is essentially a roundabout way of confirming that Workspace and Photos data may inform ads. If you interact with AI Mode while Personal Intelligence is enabled, there’s a chance that summaries and insights from your data will inform the answers you get. Because that same data is used for ad targeting, it’s accurate to say that your personal data is an element of ad targeting in AI search. The privacy policy now makes that clear.
A Google spokesperson tells Ars that its privacy clarification does not indicate a change in how it handles your data with respect to its advertising partners. It’s not scanning your entire inbox to enhance your advertising profile, and it’s not giving any of this data to third parties. But if you pipe personal data into an AI search tool, the ads it shows you could be based on that information.
The core of the problem is that Google wants its products and services to talk to each other. Google sees that wealth of data as a key strength of its AI efforts. Some apps like Gmail are still given protected status in Google’s data handling, but there are now more avenues for that data to get out. The more data you share across Google’s ecosystem, the greater the risk to your privacy.
We’ve seen a similar exception in the way Google uses your AI interactions for model training . While Google says it doesn’t use personal data for AI training, it does use your inputs and the model outputs for that purpose. With Gemini integrated with so many services and connected to them via Personal Intelligence, those outputs may very well contain elements of your personal information. Google has said it tries to filter that content from the user activity controls, therefore keeping it out of training sets. However, it doesn’t promise it will always be successful.
Google is correct that Personal Intelligence is opt-in, but the company uses various prompts and pop-ups to entice users to turn it on without fully explaining the consequences. You may have turned it on without realizing.
If you want to ensure ads never use your personal data in this way, you’ll need to make sure Personal Intelligence is turned off. The easiest way is to access the Gemini settings for Personal Intelligence and disable the connected apps. These settings are also a few levels deep in your main Google account settings under Data & privacy > Personalization settings > Manage Personalized Recommendations in Search Services > Connected Content Apps. From there, you can disable connections to Workspace and Google Photos.

articles.title_zh: Apple Store Pickup for iPhone Duo Starting to Resume But Very Limited
articles.content_orig:
The option to reserve an iPhone Duo for Apple Store pickup is starting to return on Apple's online store, with the system live again in countries such as Australia , China , Japan , and South Korea . Unfortunately, our spot check revealed extremely limited availability right now, with few to no time slots available for all configurations.
We only managed to find a single iPhone Duo unit available for Apple Store pickup in Australia on Saturday at the time we checked, as shown in the screenshot below, but it already disappeared by time we published this story.
In other countries, such as the U.S. , Canada , the U.K. , and Singapore , Apple's online store continues to advise customers to check back on Saturday, October 24 in regards to Apple Store pickup, so we expect the reservation system to resume in additional countries as the clock rolls over to Saturday time zone by time zone.
Just hours after iPhone Duo pre-orders began last Friday, Apple said demand for the device was " nothing short of extraordinary ," with delivery estimates pushing into late January, so it is not surprising that Apple Store pickup slots are hard to come by right now. Apple said it was working to satisfy demand "as quickly as possible."
Apple Store pickup was briefly offered for a few minutes after iPhone Duo pre-orders began last Friday, but the option quickly disappeared.
Given the scarcity, long queues formed at many Apple Stores around the world today, with some lucky customers managing to secure an iPhone Duo on a walk-in basis. If you were not so lucky, the Apple Store pickup tool may be your next best option, so keep an eye on the iPhone Duo order page over the next day or so and refresh often.

articles.title_orig: Dow tumbles more than 600 points as oil prices rise and market sell-off hits most sectors
articles.title_zh: Dow tumbles more than 600 points as oil prices rise and market sell-off hits most sectors
articles.content_orig:
The Dow slid on Friday as a sell-off in tech in the prior session shifted to other areas of the market and U.S. oil prices topped $100 a barrel amid rising fears that the U.S.-Iran conflict would flare up again.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 652.82 points, or 1.23%, to settle at 52,215.16, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.52% to 7,623.68. The Nasdaq Composite lost 0.21% to close at 25,955.34.
More defensive stocks came under pressure on Friday, with the consumer staples, utilities and healthcare sectors all lower. Dow component American Express fell more than 3% after announcing it was cutting about 5% of its global workforce , citing the need to "prepare for AI." Caterpillar also edged down about 2%, while Goldman Sachs lost more than 1%, adding pressure to the 30-stock index.
On Thursday, many technology stocks had pulled back as traders assessed the impact of outsized corporate borrowing and rising rates on AI and other tech names. Microsoft ticked higher on Friday. However, chip stocks such as Micron Technology and Advanced Micro Devices made a stronger move, with gains of nearly 3% and almost 2%, respectively.
"For the last two weeks, investors have been sprinting from tech stocks and data center beneficiary stocks to safe stuff, and eventually, you run out of people willing to do that sprint, and that's what today looks like and feels like," Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management, told CNBC.
Ellerbroek added that tech companies' earnings have proven strong this season, giving investors a reason to embrace tech stocks and focus less on emotion-based flights to safety.
"Emotion and fear play a really big role," the investor said. But, "we've gotten a few tech companies' [latest quarterly financial reports] and their earnings results have been good."
The 10-year Treasury yield was at around 4.999%, up more than 4 basis points on the day. The benchmark yield had fallen below the key 5% level on Thursday for the first time in a month as investors grew cautious about the massive borrowing that is underway to finance the building of AI data centers.
Oil prices also rose on Friday, further pressuring stocks. West Texas Intermediate futures were up 3.8% to settle at $103.27 per barrel. Brent crude prices rose 3.1% to end the session at $116.72 for the highest settle since April. The gains follow reports that the U.S. and Israel may be drawing up plans for renewed attacks on Iran as part of the regional war that started in late February. Iran has countered that it is prepared to strike back as well.
On the week, the S&P 500 lost 0.5%, and the Nasdaq shed 0.7%. The Dow gained 0.4% in the period.
The three major stock indexes ended Friday's session with losses.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 1.23%, or 652.82 points, to finish at 52,215.16. The S&P 500 ended down 0.52% at 7,623.68. The Nasdaq Composite closed down 0.21% at 25,955.34.
Shares of discount retailers are lower today after analysts at Wells Fargo warned in a note that rising diesel prices could pressure profits through the second half of the year and into 2027.
With third-quarter diesel prices up about 60% year-over-year, analysts estimate the average hit to operating margin will rise to about 27 basis points from 18 basis points in the second quarter. The drag on earnings per share is expected to more than double to 6.2%.
Dollar Tree and Dollar General are down around 5% in midday trading while Five Below and TJX Companies are both down more than 1% on the day. Wells Fargo says Dollar Tree is the most exposed, historically seeing a larger drag than peers when diesel spikes. They estimate the higher fuel costs will weigh on third-quarter profit by about $25 million, or 50 basis points of margin.
The increased costs could mean additional pressure on retail inflation.
Bank of America raised its price target on ServiceNow to $180, implying roughly 15% upside from Thursday's close.
BofA analyst Tal Liani reiterated his buy rating ahead of the company's third-quarter earnings on October 28, citing growing demand for its artificial intelligence offerings.
"We believe ServiceNow's AI could see broader adoption and incremental spend, which should support durable revenue growth," Liani wrote in a Friday note.
The bank's October CIO survey showed that nearly 36% of respondents expect to allocate more than 10% of their software budgets to AI, while nearly 55% said they were likely or very likely to use ServiceNow for back-office AI applications.
The analyst expects third-quarter subscription revenue to grow nearly 21% year over year as IT, customer service, and security adopt new AI products and automation tools.
Uranium, nuclear and clean energy exchange-traded funds all fell to 52-week lows on Friday, while the largest fossil fuel producers in the nation touched all-time highs.
Global X Uranium ETF and Sprott Uranium Miners ETF both dropped to their lowest levels since June 2025, while the VanEck Uranium and Nuclear ETF was at its lowest since May 2025. Of the stocks inside those ETFs, Centrus Energy , Oklo , NuScale Power , Energy Fuels and BWX Technologies were also at 52-week lows Friday.
Clean energy ETFs saw losses, too. Invesco Solar ETF and Invesco WilderHill Clean Energy ETF were at their lowest since September and August last year, respectively, while individual stocks in the group, such as NextPower , Solv Energy , Rivian Automotive and Fluence Energy , also dropped to 52-week lows.
Meanwhile, ExxonMobil , Chevron and ConocoPhillips all traded at all-time highs on Friday.
— Scott Schnipper, Gina Francolla
In a Friday note to clients, Goldman Sachs posed some key questions about hyperscaler Oracle's AI strategy as pressures mount on the AI trade and investors grow increasingly wary to part with capital.
Analyst Gabriela Borges at Goldman said the conversation around Oracle is centering on monetization in proportion to capital expenditures; the sustainability of demand amid customer concentration; and the company's ability to execute despite political pressures facing the data center buildout.
Borges has a buy rating on the stock and a price target of $206, implying upside of 64.1% compared to a closing price recorded as $125.54.
Among the key risks to the company listed by Goldman are "intense capex investment cycle and financing needs."
"Oracle has outlined a FY27 financing framework supported by roughly $20bn of equity issuance (ATM program, already executed), $20 – 25 bn of customer prepayments ($11 bn as of 1Q), ~$20bn of debt issuance (expected in 2HFY27), with the remainder funded through operating cash flow," Borges wrote.
Stocks outside the AI trade are taking the lead.
The S&P 500 Excluding AI index closed Thursday up 12.4% this year, edging out the S&P 500's roughly 12% gain. The gap has converged largely in October.
The ex-AI index is up about 6.6% in October, while the S&P 500, weighed down by concerns around AI financing, is down roughly 0.4%.
The move suggests some leadership broadening beyond AI-linked mega cap names that have dominated in recent periods. By sector, Energy and Consumer Staples are each up double digits in October while Information Technology and Communication Services lead lower, each down more than 5%.
Morgan Stanley reduced its price target on CoreWeave to $70 from $99 Friday, citing mounting financial pressures the so-called neocloud company is facing. The new target still implies 26% upside from Thursday's close.
Shares of CoreWeave, down 2% on Friday, have sold off over the past week amid investor fears over its massive artificial intelligence-rated debt. Its bond yields have also jumped, while the spread on its credit default swaps — which are insurance against default — has widened to levels generally considered distressed.

articles.title_orig: Archer to Launch Air Taxis in Texas
articles.title_zh: Archer to Launch Air Taxis in Texas
articles.content_orig:
There could soon be a new way to travel across Houston without sitting in traffic, with electric air taxis connecting major airports, downtown and Galveston.
Archer Aviation, a California aerospace company, which has discussed bringing its electric air taxis to the city, now has laid out a Houston network with named airports and destinations.
Archer's planned air taxi network in Houston would link George Bush Intercontinental Airport, William P. Hobby Airport and Sugar Land Regional Airport with the Thompson Hotel by Hyatt's helipad downtown and Galveston. The company also plans to create air taxi networks in Austin and Dallas-Fort Worth. The networks would use a 12-propeller all-electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft called the Midnight air taxi.
Archer Aviation's Houston map showing the proposed air-taxi network. (Archer Aviation)
Demonstration flights could begin as early as next year, with Houston, Dallas and Austin as focus areas, said Nikhil Goel, chief commercial officer at Archer Aviation.
Meanwhile, Sugar Land Regional Airport is pursuing a vertiport design project that could begin in 2028, Director of Aviation Mitchell Davies said, with a goal of operations beginning in by 2030.
United opens new IAH Terminal B concourse as Houston hub prepares for more growth
"Sugar Land Regional Airport is actively preparing for the future of Advanced Air Mobility (AAM) and the introduction of electric air taxis in the Greater Houston region," Davies said in a statement. "These efforts position Sugar Land Regional Airport to play a key role in bringing this emerging technology to the Houston region, providing new transportation opportunities, and enhancing regional connectivity."
Archer's all-electric Midnight aircraft could reduce some 60- to 90-minute drives to airports, business districts and other destinations to 10- to 20-minute flights, according to the announcement. Goel said the company is targeting fares similar to Uber Black pricing, with estimated costs of $100 or more, depending on distance.
The company says it is trying to combat heavy traffic in Houston, noting that congestion costs Texas commuters billions of dollars each year. In the Houston region alone, road congestion cost nearly $7.3 billion in 2024 , according to the Texas A&M Transportation Institute's 2025 Urban Mobility Report.
Archer says it is developing its Texas networks in preparation for potential operations under the White House's eVTOL Integration Pilot Program . The U.S. Department of Transportation and the Federal Aviation Administration selected the Texas Department of Transportation to lead the state program, which is using partnerships with aircraft companies to test advanced air mobility operations and develop regional air taxi flights.
"It created a pathway for us to go fly in states prior to certification," Goel said.
Archer's announcement comes as the company expands its efforts in autonomous aviation. In August, Archer announced an agreement to acquire Boeing subsidiaries Wisk Aero, SkyGrid and Insitu, a deal that would add Wisk's autonomous flight technology to Archer's portfolio. Wisk has designed, built, and flown six generations of electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft , according to Boeing and Archer in the August announcement.
In September, Archer said a federal antitrust waiting period for the transaction had expired, although other regulatory approvals and closing conditions remained. The transaction is expected to close by the end of 2026.
Goel said Archer has worked with public and private partners across Houston, and has earned the praise of U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz.
"The race to dominate next-generation aviation is moving faster than ever. Archer Aviation is a prime example of American innovation, demonstrating that the United States has what it takes to be the global standard," Cruz said. "These three planned networks will not only allow Texans to reclaim their time but also strengthen American leadership in the skies."

articles.title_orig: Ukrainian negotiator says local humanitarian ceasefire with Russia will start Tuesday
articles.title_zh: Ukrainian negotiator says local humanitarian ceasefire with Russia will start Tuesday
articles.content_orig:
WASHINGTON (AP) — First lady Melania Trump has brokered a coming ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the ravaged, Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky so that humanitarian aid can be delivered and civilians can be evacuated from a place she said is “on the brink of disaster.”
The localized ceasefire is set to begin next week.
Ukrainian, Russian and U.S. negotiators reached a deal Friday to provide humanitarian relief to the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in the war-divided region of Kherson in southern Ukraine.
Melania Trump, who worked with officials from both countries on a separate matter, initiated talks about Oleshky after learning about the situation at one of her events during the U.N. General Assembly session in September, the White House said in announcing her involvement.
She and a representative worked directly with Russian and Ukrainian leadership to define the terms of the ceasefire, the White House said.
Ukraine’s top negotiator in the effort told The Associated Press that a local ceasefire with Russia will start Tuesday — two days before the mission begins — and last several days.
Dmytro Lubinets, the Ukrainian ombudsman and his country’s chief negotiator in the talks, said the ceasefire would take effect across the Kherson region and neighboring areas essential to the operation. He added the initiative could act as a model for future humanitarian missions.
Russian officials also confirmed the agreement.
Lubinets earlier Friday thanked Melania Trump and said the deal would be tough to accomplish. He said the agreement calls for a ceasefire, followed by the delivery of much-needed humanitarian aid. Lastly, civilians will be allowed to leave Oleshky, he said in a video message posted online.
“The operation will be carried out gradually and is extremely challenging to implement,” Lubinets said.
Lubinets said the operation would involve removing mines on the way to Oleshky before the physical delivery of humanitarian supplies and the arranging of evacuations.
He gave no further details on how the ceasefire or the aid mission would be monitored or implemented, citing the sensitivity of the negotiations. He declined to comment when asked if Melania Trump would travel to Ukraine.
“When Melania Trump learned about the situation in Oleshky, the negotiation process began under her coordination,” he said. “For several weeks, we discussed many questions, initiatives and ideas. We established new approaches, mechanisms and tools to do everything possible to help civilians in Oleshky survive.”
Russia’s chief of the general staff, Gen. Valery Gerasimov, said Russian forces “will cease fire on the Kherson axis” starting at 4 a.m. Tuesday in Moscow” — or late Monday in the United States — “in connection with the humanitarian operation near Oleshky.”
Russian forces will also carry out “engineering reconnaissance” and ensure “safe movement of the humanitarian convoy” into the city, Gerasimov said.
Russia’s human rights ombudswoman, Yana Lantratova, confirmed that Melania Trump had brokered an agreement on “organizing a humanitarian mission” in Oleshky. Lantratova, who said she participated in negotiations, said providing such assistance is Russia’s priority.
The first step will be to clarify what people need and organize the delivery of food, medicine, hygiene products and other essentials, Lantratova said in an online statement. Safe passage will be guaranteed for anyone who wants to leave the combat zone, she said, adding that it will require abiding by the ceasefire and creating safe conditions for humanitarian vehicles.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Moscow was grateful to the first lady. He said Russian President Vladimir Putin and President Donald Trump had recently discussed the effort.
Peskov said “those who want to leave it would be able to do so.” He would not say whether they would be taken to Russia- or Ukraine-held territory. He also demurred when asked how long the evacuation will last, saying only it would most likely take several days.
Melania Trump has made helping children in conflict zones one of her signature issues in her husband’s second term. She hosted a U.N. Security Council meeting on the issue earlier this year, and last year wrote Putin about efforts to reunite families with children who have been displaced by the war. She has helped reunite nearly three dozen children, according to her senior adviser, Marc Beckman.
“What she wants to do is save children, and that’s her focus,” the president told reporters at the White House.
Beckman portrayed the first lady’s work on the ceasefire as an extension of her efforts to help reunite Russian and Ukrainian children with their families after they were separated by Russia’s war against Ukraine.
The development comes as tensions have increased to new highs between the Trump administration and Ukraine’s government. Kyiv has faced restrictions on the satellite internet system it relies on to knock down Russian attacks, with Trump and other top U.S. officials sending mixed messages about who was responsible for throttling the Elon Musk-made Starshield system.
Trump also recently waived new Russia sanctions , reached an agreement with Russia to import diesel fuel and pushed Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to make a deal to end the war that Russia began in February 2022. In renewed efforts to revive the peace process , Trump envoy Steve Witkoff traveled to Norway this week for talks with Zelenskyy before meeting Putin in St. Petersburg, Russia.
Zelenskyy did not mention the ceasefire in Oleshky during a remote appearance at the Hudson Institute, a Washington think tank. He did note that American Patriot missile interceptors were still on hold and Starshield and Starlink speed limits were still in place.
He also spoke of the importance of the United States to renewed diplomatic efforts to end the war, including a possible joint meeting with Trump and Putin.
Food and medical supplies have been scarce for months in Oleshky, which sits on the Dnipro River that separates Ukrainian forces from the city’s Russian occupiers. There is no electricity, heat or running water. Roads leading from town are mined and dotted with burned-out cars. Drones buzz overhead.
Once a city of about 24,000 residents, Oleshky was captured by Moscow’s forces on the first day of their full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Its buildings were shelled and burned, and its infrastructure damaged. In June 2023, floodwaters inundated the city after the Kakhovka Dam collapsed from an explosion that an Associated Press investigation found was likely caused by the Russian military. Hundreds of residents were killed.
Those left in the city along Ukraine’s southeastern front face death from hunger or disease as another harsh winter looms. Ukraine has appealed repeatedly for a local ceasefire to organize evacuations. Russia, as the occupying power, is obligated by international law to ensure civilians under its control have what they need to survive.
Associated Press writers Konstantin Toropin and Darlene Superville in Washington, Volodymyr Yurchuk, Derek Gatopoulos and Susie Blann in Kyiv, Ukraine, and Dasha Litvinova in Tallinn, Estonia, contributed to this report.

articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Oil prices climbed to a 6-month high on Friday as traders priced the odds of escalating fighting in the Middle East. Attacks near the Red Sea also stoked worries of further constraints on oil supplies from the region.
Brent crude ( BZ=F ) futures for December delivery settled at $116.72 per barrel. The international benchmark posted its third consecutive week of gains. Meanwhile, West Texas Intermediate crude ( CL=F ) closed just above $103 a barrel.
President Trump telegraphed an escalation in Iran after the midterm elections and an extended stand-off, with the Strait of Hormuz remaining at the center of the conflict.
This week, the New York Times reported that the US and Israel have reportedly drawn up plans for renewed attacks on Iran after the Nov. 3 elections. The US has ordered nonessential embassy personnel to depart Saudi Arabia after a series of attacks at the country's airports and oil fields .
President Trump has said he will not attack Iran before the midterms and has suggested that fuel prices will fall afterward.
Meanwhile, the Red Sea area has seen increased attacks recently, including on Saudi Arabian airports and on an Aramco oil field this week.
Saudi Aramco on Thursday ordered the evacuation of its headquarters in Dhahran , marking the oil giant's first such evacuation since the Iran war began.
On Friday, the national price of gasoline stood at $4.29 per gallon, roughly $1.22 higher than a year ago. Diesel hovered around $6.31, about $2.68 more than this time last year.
A power outage at a refinery in the Chicago area is expected to send refined fuel prices even higher in the region.
"You're going to see a lot of $5 gas prices in places like Michigan, Ohio, Minnesota, Illinois, and Indiana," Gulf Oil chief energy adviser Tom Kloza told Yahoo Finance on Thursday.
Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter for Yahoo Finance.

articles.title_orig: Wolves Descend on Finnish Villages After Google Hacked Down 1,300 Acres of Habitat to Make Room for AI Data Centers
articles.title_zh: Wolves Descend on Finnish Villages After Google Hacked Down 1,300 Acres of Habitat to Make Room for AI Data Centers
articles.content_orig:
Earlier in October, Finnish authorities ordered Google’s affiliate data center developer Tuike Finland Oy to immediately suspend the illegal cutting of some 1,300 acres of forest. The tech giant was given a week to draft a report explaining its actions, which soon became a flashpoint for Europe’s growing outrage over the data center boom.
As the anger grew, reporters descended on the scene — and what they found is a clear-cut example of the AI revolution’s impact on the environment.
New reporting by the Guardian shed fresh light on the impacts of Google’s deforestation. After the 1,300 acres of pristine boreal forests were reduced to tracts of mud and stumps, fauna which once called the woods home has been forced to vacate.
In the felling-site near the Finnish village of Otanmäki, the ensuing loss of prey has forced packs of wolves to search for food elsewhere: nearby villages.
“We had wolves coming into the village because all the wild animals moved out of the forest,” 53-year-old Otanmäki resident Anni Ranta told the Guardian . “They fled.”
Though Ranta’s family has called the area home for generations, the tumult has her considering whether to move out of Otanmäki for good.
“I don’t want them here,” she continued, speaking of Google’s data centers. “I don’t want them in Finland at all. I don’t like the whole idea of AI and the world changing and the way it’s changing. It’s going too fast, too soon.”
Antti Jakonen, a resident of Muhos, put it in even starker terms. “It has been done in the wrong way. American style. No sense. No sense at all,” he told the Guardian .
Sure enough, back in Google’s home country, data center developers are increasingly duking it out with the natural world — and winning handily.
In West Virginia, a grove of critically endangered Chestnut trees is under threat of being bulldozed to make way for a new Anthropic hyperscale facility. Outside of Fort Wayne, a chunk of Indiana’s once-bountiful wetlands is being tilled to fit a new Google data center. In Southern New Jersey, a data center operator was recently slapped with a $1 million fine after inspectors uncovered 62 illegal gas generators belching exhaust into the surrounding environment.
Wherever in the world data centers go up, it seems the destruction of natural resources is inevitable — and increasingly difficult for humanity to ignore.

articles.title_orig: Trump's executive order targets mortgage insurance, refinance costs. What it means for borrowers
articles.title_zh: Trump's executive order targets mortgage insurance, refinance costs. What it means for borrowers
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump has signed an executive order that aims to reduce mortgage costs as rising interest rates and inflation make homeownership less affordable .
The order , titled "Decreasing Housing Costs for the American People," directs federal agencies to proactively cancel mortgage insurance on eligible future loans and expand a program to make refinancing cheaper, among other actions.
In an X post on Thursday , Federal Housing Finance Agency director Bill Pulte said "millions of Americans will save thousands and thousands of dollars."
But it's difficult to know the future consumer impact without more details, according to Keith Gumbinger, vice president of mortgage website HSH.
Trump's executive order comes less than two weeks before the Nov. 3 midterm elections , with rising costs and housing affordability a major concern among voters. It builds on previous orders to restrict Wall Street firms from buying single-family homes, among other actions.
Homeownership has become less affordable in recent years. In 2025, the monthly payment for a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage on a median-priced home was roughly 33% of the median family's income, up from 26% in 2022, according to the Federal Reserve's latest Survey of Consumer Finances published in early October.
Whether you're a current homeowner or future buyer, here are some of the key things to know about the new executive order.
Conventional loans — mortgages not insured or backed by U.S. government programs — typically require private mortgage insurance, or PMI, when a down payment is less than 20% of the home's purchase price. By contrast, Federal Housing Administration mortgages require mortgage insurance on all loans.
Trump's executive order directs the FHFA to create a pilot program that cancels eligible borrowers' mortgage insurance "proactively" once their home equity reaches a certain threshold, according to the White House. This would apply to mortgages originated after the pilot program launches.
Currently, conventional loan borrowers can generally remove PMI once their loan balance is below 80% of the purchase price or once they have reached 20% equity, according to Fannie Mae. Once your balance reaches 80% of the original value, you can ask your loan servicer if you're eligible to remove PMI, or they may remove it automatically when your balance reaches 78% of the original value.
In a statement Thursday , Seth Appleton, president of U.S. mortgage insurers, an industry trade organization, said: "We commend the President's focus on lowering costs for future homeowners, and the private mortgage insurance industry is proud to already be delivering on that goal."
Typically, the cost of PMI can be 0.2% to 2% of the loan annually , but varies based on your down payment size, credit score, amount borrowed and other factors, according to Fannie Mae.
For example, if you purchased a $600,000 home with a 10% down payment and a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage at 7.3%, your monthly mortgage insurance could be $351, according to a private mortgage calculator from Freddie Mac.
"Most mortgages ... are carrying PMI at this point in time, especially with the way home prices have been and down payments being as small as they've been in recent years," Gumbinger said.
During the second quarter of 2026, the median home down payment was 13.7% of the home's purchase price, or $27,100, according to a September report from Realtor.com.
Trump's executive order also aims to reduce mortgage refinancing costs by making permanent the FHFA's pilot program that waives the lender's title insurance policy and allows "cost-friendly alternatives," according to the White House.
"I don't know that it's necessarily a game-changer in terms of the cost of housing, which is dictated by home price and mortgage rates at the moment," Gumbinger said. "But you know, every little bit certainly helps."
As of Oct. 23, mortgage interest rates for 30-year fixed-rate mortgages were 7.32%, according to Freddie Mac, and refinance demand was down 59% in mid-October, compared with the same week the previous year.
Originally planned through November 2027, the FHFA pilot was "limited in scope," for refinances with a loan-to-value ratio below 80%, in a handful of states, former FHFA director Sandra Thompson said during a congressional hearing in April 2024.
Thompson estimated that consumers could save $500 to $1,500 in closing costs for loans sold under the pilot program.
Making the program permanent could save borrowers because the lender's title insurance policy, which is usually required for new loans and refinances, "has always been fairly pricey," Gumbinger said.
The lender's fees related to title and title insurance generally make up the largest share of mortgage closing costs , according to a 2025 Urban Institute report.
